title: DevExp roadmap reality-check: SDKs, samples, quickstarts
content:
Meeting: DevExp — Roadmap reality-check (informal)
Date: 2026-07-20
Facilitator: Aisha
Attendees: Aisha, Marcus, Priya, Diego, Lena, optional: Kim
Duration: 45m (ran +10)

Purpose:
- Quick reality-check vs. roadmap for SDKs, samples and quickstarts before Eng offsite.
- Surface blockers that would cause slip on the public quickstart library and the sample app demo.

Agenda:
1) Quick status updates (5m each): SDKs, samples repo, guided quickstarts
2) Risks & blockers
3) Prioritization: what must land before offsite demo
4) Action-items and owners

Notes / Highlights:
- SDKs
  - Python 0.8.1 release candidate in CI, but a couple async tests flaky on ppc64 (we only run x86 in CI). Marcus to open follow-up flaky test ticket. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/412
  - JS/TS SDK: initial function-calling ergonomics merged, but docs surface is incomplete. Priya proposed a short one-page guide: "function-calls-quickstart.md" for docs site.
  - Mobile bindings: internal spike showed decent perf for iOS (Catalyst) but need a decision on packaging (Carthage vs SPM). Tentative: SPM. Action: Diego to draft packaging proposal.

- Samples & Quickstarts
  - samples-repo has 12 new quickstarts in draft. We want 6 polished quickstarts for the offsite demo (one per use-case: chat, summarization, reranking, embeddings-search, code-assist, multimodal stub).
  - Biggest gap: an end-to-end embedding + vector DB quickstart that uses Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching) — currently a half-complete notebook. Lena will pair with Solutions Eng to finish.
  - Quickstart execution time: average cold-start for the JS sample is 18s (too long). Identified startup script that fetches large model metadata synchronously — change to async and cache. Marcus owns.

- Docs & Examples site
  - Confluence plan exists but public docs need to match. We must avoid duplicate narratives. Decision: publish quickstart-first guides directly in docs site and link to Confluence for internal design notes.
  - Action: Priya to write a 1-pager for the docs lead summarizing the tone + minimal code snippets (deadline: 2026-07-26).

Risks & Blockers (top ones):
- CI flakiness on SDK tests (ppc64) could delay release candidate. Workaround: skip flaky suites for the RC and fix post-ship (bad, but acceptable if communicated).
- Sample cold-starts for JS demo: impacts demo quality. Need a fix in 72h.
- Vector DB quickstart needs a stable small dataset and local runner. Without it, the demo will rely on a mock end-to-end which is less convincing.

Prioritization (what must land before offsite demo):
- Fix JS cold-start (Marcus) — high
- Finish embedding quickstart + add small hosted dataset (Lena + Solutions Eng) — high
- Publish "function calls" quickstart page and code sample (Priya) — medium-high
- Mobile packaging proposal (Diego) — low-medium (informational for roadmap only)

Decisions made:
- Publish quickstarts as "stable" if they pass the nightly smoke runner (not full CI). This lets us ship incremental fixes post-offsite.
- Use SPM for iOS packaging experimental branch (if packaging proposal OK).

Action Items (owner — due):
- Marcus: Open flaky-test ticket, implement async metadata fetch in JS startup script, create smoke-run job for samples (due 2026-07-23)
- Priya: Draft docs one-pager + function-calls-quickstart.md for docs site (due 2026-07-26)
- Lena: Pair with Solutions Eng to finish embedding quickstart and create small sample dataset + vector DB runner (due 2026-07-24)
- Diego: Draft iOS packaging proposal and risk notes (due 2026-07-28)
- Aisha: Prepare offsite demo checklist and backup plan (use mock demo) (due 2026-07-25)

Open questions / parking lot:
- Do we include an "optimize" panel in the demo that shows real-time cost breakdown? (UX asks: needs token breakouts wired.)
- Should quickstarts live in samples-repo or in docs repo as canonical copies? (Decision leaning to docs as canonical + samples-repo as runnable clones.)
- Who is on-call for offsite demo day? Need a rotations page.

Corrigenda / Quick wins flagged in meeting:
- Convert large synchronous fetch to local metadata cache in JS startup — saves ~12s on cold start.
- Add a smoke runner that exercises each quickstart's happy path in under 30s; useful for presubmit gating.

References / Links discussed:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/412
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEVEX/quickstart-library-v2
- Jira: DEVEXP-287 (samples smoke runner)
- Slack: #devexp (thread about quickstart tone)

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep offsite demo minimal and confident — fewer things that can fail live.
- Prioritize small, polished examples over many half-baked ones.
- Remember to take screenshots of the embedding demo flow for the press kit.

Follow-up meeting: informal sync Friday 2026-07-23 10:00 PT to check status of Marcus/Lena fixes. Invite list: Aisha, Marcus, Lena, Priya.

End of notes.
